say: "Rain again, huh. Third week running."
"Do you know a good place for melon bread around here?"
"Is it always this quiet after the 5 o'clock chime?"
"I'm new. Asagiri. From the sweet shop."
"Nice day for it. ...Whatever 'it' is."
"Have you lived in Suzunari long?"
"The cats here stare a lot, don't they?"

lines: "Honestly? Nobody's asked me anything in weeks. I'm {job_a}. It's... a job."
"#chatter#" They seem glad somebody listened.
"The Suzunari Seagulls lost again. I put a hundred yen on them every week. It's loyalty, not betting."
"I'm {job_a}. Don't ask what it pays. It pays in leftover dango."
"Somebody wrote '#graffiti#' on the wall by my place. I've started to agree with it."
"Rain again. My laundry's been on the line since Tuesday. It's wetter than when I washed it."

say: "You look busy. Need a hand with anything?"
"Is something wrong? You keep looking at your phone."
"Anything I can do? I'm free till the bell."
"You dropped something - oh. You didn't. Need help, though?"
"Here. For the vending machine. Don't argue."
"Take it. Pay me back in melon bread someday."
"For the train fare. Go home, it's getting dark."

lines: "...No catch? Is this a prank show?" They pocket it fast, before the world changes its mind.
"I'll pay you back. I won't, but I'll think about it."
They bow so low their glasses slide off. "I'll light a stick of incense for you. Two."

say: "Let me buy you a yakisoba bread. I insist."
"Konbini onigiri? My treat. Tuna mayo or salmon?"
"There's a ramen stand by the station. I'm paying."

lines: They eat like they haven't had a hot meal since spring. "I owe you. Here's something nobody's supposed to know..."
Melon bread from the konbini, still warm. They tear it in half and give you the bigger piece. "Listen. Between us..."

say: "Want half my bento? My aunt packs too much."
"Itadakimasu - here, try the tamagoyaki."
"I've got two rice balls and one stomach."
"Heard anything weird around town lately?"
"What's the story with the shrine on the hill?"
"Is it true about the 1000th step?"
"Who's the girl in the red kimono near my aunt's shop?"

lines: "You hear things down here, right? Me too. Swap?"
They lower their voice to the level the cats can't hear.
"Gossip? Me? Never." They look both ways first, though.

say: "Tell people the Asagiri sweet shop has a new mochi."
"If anyone asks - I'm just a normal guy. Spread that around."
"Could you put in a good word for me? With... everyone?"

lines: "Oh, I'm telling EVERYONE. My cousin runs the shopping street group chat."
"By tonight the whole queue at the noodle stall will know."
"Leave it with me. By tomorrow even the jizo will know."
"And have the whole street know I said it? No thanks."
"I'll keep that one to myself, if it's all the same."

ask_reputation.text: Ask what people say about you
say: "What do people say about me? Be honest."
"Am I the guy from the Ura board? Don't answer that. ...Am I?"
"Do people think I'm weird? Scale of one to Kuroe-senpai."
"That hairpin suits you. Seriously."
"You've got a great laugh, you know that?"
"I'd remember a face like yours. ...I'm bad with faces. But I'd remember."
"Your handwriting on the notice board is the nicest one."
"Why did the kappa fail his exam? He kept losing his head-water."
"I asked the maneki-neko for luck. It waved goodbye."
"My aunt says I'm sweet. Occupational hazard."
"Knock knock. - Who's there? - Hanako. - ...Oh no."

lines: "Why did the kappa cross the road? To get to the other cucumber." It's terrible. They laugh anyway, then hate themselves.
Your joke is so bad it loops back to good. They're laughing too hard to stay cross with you.
Silence. Somewhere a crow laughs instead. Somehow that's worse.

say: "I'm actually a transfer student from Tokyo. Big shot. Very cool."
"I'm allergic to cats. Very allergic. Tell the cats."
"Me? I've never been to this town before in my life."
"The teacher said there's no homework this week."
"Can I tell you something? I'm scared of this town."
"I have dreams about a man in 1868. Every night."
"I think something's following me. Something small. With ears."

lines: "Thanks for telling me. I'm going to tell everybody."

say: "Sorry about earlier. That was out of line."
"I'm really sorry. I'll make it up to you, promise. ...Wait, not promise."
"Gomen. I mean it."

lines: "An apology? From a teenager? I need to sit down."
"...Okay. Thanks. Nobody says sorry here. They just bring round mikan."
They soften. "We all have bad days. Yours are just louder."
"Sorry doesn't fix my shutter."
"Tell it to the shrine."

say: "Rough day? Yeah. Me too."
"Exams, rain, and cats. This town, huh."
"It'll be okay. ...I don't know that. But it might."

lines: You compare how many days it's rained. They win. You both laugh until the awning drips on you.
"#thing.cap# went up again." "Mine too." A whole friendship, built on complaining.
They share a trick: the bakery puts out yesterday's melon bread at seven, round the back. Free.

say: "You can do it. Seriously - I've seen you try."
"Don't give up on it. Things in this town have waited longer."
"If you want to leave and become a manga artist - go. Write about us."

lines: "Change? In Suzunari? The last change here was the bus timetable, in 1994."

say: "Is there someone you like? You can tell me."
"How do you know when someone likes you? Asking for a... cat."
"Tanabata's coming. Got someone to wish for?"

lines: "Everyone here has lost someone. The sea's greedy like that."

say: "Wow. Did you get dressed in the dark?"
"Your bike bell is the most annoying sound in Suzunari."
"You talk like the station announcement. Slow and wrong."

lines: "Ha! Finally someone says it. I've been thinking it for forty years."
They lean in. "Keep talking like that and the old women will hear. I like you."
"I'm telling your aunt."
"Rude. My grandmother would have thrown salt at you."

say: "Back off. Now."
"Say that again and see what happens."
"I know where the 1000th step is. Want to go there?"

lines: "Okay, okay! I don't want trouble. I can't afford trouble."
They go pale. "Fine. Fine! Just - not in front of the shrine."
They laugh. Actually laugh. That hurts more than a punch.
"Threatening me? I raised four sons. Try harder."

say: (Bump into them. "Ah - sorry!")
(Ask the time while your hand moves.)
(Point at a cat on the roof. "Look!")

lines: "HEY! THIEF! Somebody call the police! Somebody call his AUNT!"
Their hand clamps on your wrist. "That's my shopping money, you little tanuki."

say: "Come on, a little discount for a local?"
"My aunt runs Asagiri-do. Neighbours' price?"
"Two for the price of one? It's raining."

lines: "Haggling? In this economy?" The price goes UP.

deliver_message.text: Offer to pass on a message
say: "I've got a note for you. From... a friend."
"Someone asked me to give you this. Don't ask who."

lines: "Could you get this to my sister in the next town? The post office here loses things. On purpose, I think." You pocket it. You never look inside.

say: "Bon-odori practice? Teach me the steps."
"Dance with me. Nobody's watching. ...The cats are watching."

lines: They spin, you spin, a cat watches with deep disapproval. "Worth it."
"I haven't danced since the Obon festival... last year." They're laughing.

rebel: delinquent with a heart of gold
weird: person who talks to the vending machine

poor: A day without rain, so the laundry dries
My grandson to call. Just once
Someone to fix the shop shutter
A winning lottery ticket. A small one
worker: A boss who goes home before me
The last bus to wait for me, just once
artsy: A wall I'm allowed to paint
One customer who buys a painting instead of a postcard
The light at Omagatoki, in a jar
corporate: Proof my manager takes long lunches
Someone to blame for the quarterly report
rebel: A town that stays up past nine
My bike back. Someone took my bike
weird: A cucumber the kappa hasn't touched
To find out what's in the sealed tunnel
A ghost who answers questions properly
